guide_title: How to extract Kinect Adventures photos
guide_step1:
1. Put the photo saves on a USB drive
In Xbox 360 Storage/Memory settings, open the device holding your Kinect Adventures! photo saves and copy them to a USB drive. If the saves are already on an external USB drive, continue with that drive. Older dashboards list Storage under My Xbox.
guide_step2:
2. Copy the files in File Explorer
Connect the USB drive to your PC and open it in File Explorer. Copy its Content folder, or the Kinect Adventures folder inside it, to a normal folder on your PC. If Content is not visible, turn on View > Hidden items. On newer Xbox 360 USB storage, these files can be copied directly; no Xbox storage tool is needed.
guide_step3:
3. Check what you copied
Photo saves normally appear below Content/<profile>/4D5308ED/00000001 and start with PM9_. They do not have to end in .jpg. 4D5308ED is Kinect Adventures!' game ID. Copying the whole Content folder is fine. If Windows cannot show the files on an older Xbox USB drive, see the legacy-format note below. This app cannot read raw disk images.
guide_step4:
4. Open the copied folder here
Click Open Kinect Adventures files and select the main copied folder, Content, 4D5308ED, or 00000001. Choose an Export folder, review the discovered photos, then click Extract selected.
guide_legacy:
Older Xbox USB format (XTAF)
Some drives configured with the older Xbox-managed format may not show individual saves in File Explorer, even with Hidden items enabled. Use a compatible storage browser such as USB XTAF Explorer (gruntmods.com/usb-xtaf-explorer) to copy the Kinect Adventures files or Content folder to your PC. It is a discontinued legacy utility. Do not format the drive to extract photos. Whether a tool is needed depends on the drive format, not the age of the photos.
